text:
maria.chen: FYI BrightCart reported a spike of 503/429s this morning, looks correlated with dedicated pool scaling events. raising here.
ashok: saw the alert, digging into autoscaler logs now.
support-eng: customer says errors are intermittent for 10-15m windows, then clears. they were on dedicated/gpu-pool-7.
devon: do we have timestamps and example request ids from BrightCart? need repro.
support-eng: forwarded a sample request id: bc-req-58a3. attached their SDK logs — lots of short retries.
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2025-839. severity: high. assigned to eng-sre.
ashok: brief triage: scale events at 10:02, 10:06, 10:09 UTC. metrics show scale-up -> scale-down -> scale-up (3 cycles in 10m).
kendra: that smells like oscillation. what metric is the autoscaler using for pool-7? core metric is "pending_queue_length" with 30s window.
jules: 30s is pretty aggressive for bursty traffic. also cooldown configured at 60s.
ashok: grabbing prometheus snippets:

```
# pending queue peak around events
sum(rate(dedicated_request_queue_length[1m])) by (pool)
pool="gpu-pool-7" -> spikes to ~220 at 10:01:50 then drops under 20 by 10:02:40
```

ashok: CPU/GPU utilization stayed ~40-60% during spikes — not saturated, but scheduling latency for new nodes ~15-25s.
maria.chen: scheduling latency + short smoothing probably causes scaler to see spike -> scale -> by the time capacity ready spike gone -> scale down -> repeat.
devon: also check noisy neighbor effects: some instances showed high memory pressure causing evictions on a few pods.
support-eng: customer reports increased 429s (throttles) when scale events happen.

kendra: proposed immediate mitigations:
- increase smoothing window from 30s -> 2m
- bump cooldown from 60s -> 300s
- set min_replicas for gpu-pool-7 to 4 (they were at 1)
- temporarily enable request-queue backpressure at router for BrightCart to reduce retries

jules: +1 on min_replicas, that will reduce cold starts. need to evaluate cost impact.
ashok: quick config diff to test in staging:

```
autoscaler:
  pool: gpu-pool-7
  metric: pending_queue_length
  smoothing_window: 120s
  cooldown: 300s
  min_replicas: 4
```

maria.chen: devon, can you run this in staging and run the reproduction script from support? link: https://internal/runbooks/brightcart-repro

devon: running now, rough repro steps I'm using:
1) seed 100 concurrent short requests over 90s
2) follow with 500 req/s burst for 30s
3) watch queue_length, scale events, request latencies

oncall-bot: staging job started: job-4973. logs here: https://ci.internal/jobs/job-4973

ashok: I also looked at scaler code — it uses instantaneous rate then applies smoothing. there's no hysteresis threshold for downscale, only a simple check: if metric < threshold -> scale down. we should add a stabilizing check like requiring sustained below-threshold for 2 windows.
kendra: agree. short-term change: increase smoothing + cooldown + min_replicas. medium-term: change algorithm to use p95 request latency as a signal and add hysteresis.

support-eng: from support POV, we need a rollback path if this causes cost/regressions. can we feature-flag the change per-pool?
jules: yes, autoscaler config is flaggable per pool. will deploy to staging -> canary to gpu-pool-7-us-east -> then global if green.

devon: staging run shows fewer oscillations after smoothing=120s + cooldown=300s, single scale-up when burst happens and then steadies. will attach graphs.
maria.chen: excellent. put the graphs into INC-2025-839 ticket and schedule a 1hr window to roll to prod tonight.

ashok: action items:
- devon: post staging graphs & replay to ticket (ETA 2h)
- jules: prepare canary deploy manifest and rollout plan (ETA 3h)
- kendra: cost estimate for min_replicas=4 for gpu-pool-7 (ETA 3h)
- support-eng: notify BrightCart about maintenance window and ask for retry backoff mitigation (ETA 30m)

support-eng: assigned a customer follow-up: we'll keep them updated. noted they asked for credit for the impacted window.
maria.chen: keep thread updated. if we see regressions after canary, revert config flag.

ashok: follow-up note: added a small debugging patch to autoscaler to log the raw metric values and decisions to aid future triage.

kendra: long term proposals to review next week:
- add percentile-latency-based scaling (p95/p99)
- incorporate node provisioning time into scaling decision
- reservation/burst pool for known large customers
- better isolation to avoid noisy neighbor evictions

maria.chen: thanks all — closing initial triage. INC-2025-839 will track next steps and RCA.
